thread:
Alice Gomez: Hey infra, onboarding a new internal account (pegasus). Need a VPC in eu-west-2 with an H100 reserved fleet (~48 GPUs). Planning multi-AZ private subnets, PrivateLink for model-registry, and NAT egress. Quick ask: subnet sizing + ENI/IP quota + NAT scaling.

Ravi Patel: Do you plan to use multiple ENIs per instance with secondary IPs? If so we need to size subnets for 3-4 IPs per GPU-host and request ENI attachment quotas.

Alice Gomez: Yes — each host will have 1 primary ENI + 2 secondary IPs for sidecars (monitoring, metrics). Estimate 3 IPs per host. We'll start with 6 nodes (8 GPUs each) and autoscale to 12 nodes. So target capacity = 12 nodes * 3 ips = 36 IPs but we need headroom for control-plane + endpoints. Wondering whether /24s per AZ are enough.

Lina Chen: /24 per AZ will be tight once you add interface endpoints, NAT instances, k8s infra, and build nodes. Recommend /22 per AZ if you expect growth and to avoid reallocating later. Also consider IP exhaustion due to ENI limits on p5 instances.

Marta Ruiz: From networking POV: provision one NAT GW per AZ for bandwidth and failover. For H100 egress (model pulls + S3) expect sustained 3-5 Gbps. Single managed NAT GW could saturate — consider ec2-based NAT autoscale behind an ALB for bursty egress and a small EIP pool.

infra-bot: Quota snapshot for account pegasus: ec2-network-interfaces = 350, vpc-elastic-ips = 20, nat-gateways per region = 5.

cloudquota-bot: Suggested increases submitted: ec2-network-interfaces -> 2000, vpc-elastic-ips -> 120, nat-gateways -> 10. Created ticket Q-9921 (https://cloud.quota.example/Q-9921).

Ravi Patel: Also file a request for 'IPv4 addresses per subnet' usage increase if provider enforces soft limits. And double-check p5.24xlarge ENI/IP behavior — per-instance ENI attachments matter for ip planning.

Alice Gomez: We'll use p5.24xlarge for H100 hosts initially. Planning k8s with CNI secondary IPs (aws-vpc-cni). Will need ENI quota and secondary ip pool headroom.

Lina Chen: p5.24xlarge supports many ENIs but the per-ENI secondary IP limit is the constraining factor. Real-world is often IP exhaustion before ENI limit. Also reserve /28s for each interface endpoint (PrivateLink) so those don't eat into host subnets.

Marta Ruiz: Action items: 1) Alice to finalize CIDR plan. 2) I'll prototype an autoscaling NAT template (ec2 NAT + EIP pool). 3) Ravi to file quota increases for ENIs/EIPs and route-table association if needed. 4) Lina to sketch PrivateLink endpoint placements and reserved /28s per endpoint.

Alice Gomez: Draft CIDR plan below — open to pushback:
```
VPC: 10.44.0.0/20
AZ1 private: 10.44.0.0/22
AZ2 private: 10.44.4.0/22
AZ3 private: 10.44.8.0/22
Public (NAT/bastion): 10.44.12.0/24
Endpoints (reserved small blocks): reserve /28s out of public/management range
```

Ravi Patel: That looks sane. /22 per AZ gives ~1024 total addresses across VPC, plenty of headroom. For ENI quota I'll request: ec2-network-interfaces=2000 and vpc-elastic-ips=120 to support an EIP pool for NAT. Also include a limit increase for interface endpoints if provider enforces a per-region cap.

cloudquota-bot: Ticket Q-9921 updated by Ravi: added 'network-interface' and 'elastic-ip' quota increases plus note to review interface endpoint quota. Estimated review 48-72 hours.

Marta Ruiz: For PrivateLink, we should use interface endpoints in private subnets and avoid routing their traffic through NAT. Reserve a /28 per endpoint in each AZ to guarantee capacity. Also add security group egress rules for registry S3 endpoints.

Alice Gomez: Cost note: 3 managed NAT Gateways + EIPs + potential ec2 NAT autoscaling ~= estimated $6k-$9k/month depending on transfer. I'll put a conservative finance estimate in the onboarding doc.

James O'Leary: If you need quicker EIP allocation, we can pre-request EIPs via support and pre-create interface endpoints to reduce NAT egress. Also check provider region-specific limits for p5 instance boot quotas.

Alice Gomez: Good call. I'll follow up with the design doc and attach the quota ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
